record.paper_title: INPUT-TO-STATE STABILITY OF INFINITE-DIMENSIONAL SYSTEMS: RECENT RESULTS AND OPEN QUESTIONS
record.original_question: Create general ISS methods for fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional PDEs, not only for linear or semilinear equations of the form ẋ = Ax + f(x,u) with a bounded nonlinear part. In particular, extend ISS analysis to important fully nonlinear PDE classes such as porous medium and Navier–Stokes type equations, where nonlinear semigroup methods may be needed.

evidence.quote: 10.3. ISS of fully nonlinear PDEs. The absolute majority of PDE systems, which have been analyzed for robustness within the ISS framework, are either linear or belong to the class of semilinear systems, which can be written in the form (2.13).

However, many important PDEs as porous medium equation [230] and Navier-Stokes equations, do not fall into this category. This calls for looking onto a more general class of infinite-dimensional problems, which will include fully nonlinear PDEs.

For systems without inputs, the theory of nonlinear semigroups [44, 122, 159] gives a powerful method for the unified study of such equations. General methods for investigation of ISS for systems from this class are highly desirable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider control systems of the form
    x'(t) = F(x(t), u(t)),  t > 0,  x(0) = x_0,
where the state x(t) takes values in a Banach space X, the input u belongs to the space U_c := L^∞(R_+, U) of essentially bounded measurable functions with values in a normed space U, and F generates (for each fixed input) a possibly nonlinear evolution. A typical existing framework treats the semilinear case
    x'(t) = A x(t) + f(x(t), u(t)),
where A generates a strongly continuous (linear) semigroup on X and f satisfies suitable Lipschitz/boundedness conditions.

A system Σ with state space X and input space U_c is called input-to-state stable (ISS) if there exist β ∈ KL and γ ∈ K such that for every initial state x_0 ∈ X, every admissible input u ∈ U_c, and all t ≥ 0,
    ‖x(t; x_0, u)‖_X ≤ β(‖x_0‖_X, t) + γ(‖u‖_{L^∞(0,t;U)}),
where K denotes continuous strictly increasing functions [0,∞) → [0,∞) vanishing at 0, and KL denotes functions β(r,t) that are class-K in r and decrease to 0 as t → ∞.

The theory of nonlinear semigroups (m-accretive operators, Crandall–Liggett generation, mild solutions in the sense of Bénilan–Crandall–Pazy) provides a unified well-posedness framework for fully nonlinear evolution equations including the porous medium equation
    ∂_t ρ = Δ(ρ^m) + b(ρ, u),  m > 1,
on a bounded domain Ω ⊂ R^d with appropriate boundary conditions and distributed/boundary input u, and the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations
    ∂_t v + (v · ∇)v = νΔv − ∇p + g(v, u),  div v = 0,
on a domain Ω with boundary conditions and an input u entering through forcing or boundary data.

Problem. Develop a general theory of input-to-state stability for fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional control systems generated by (perturbed) nonlinear semigroups on Banach spaces. Specifically:

(a) Formulate sufficient conditions, expressed in terms of the nonlinear generator F (e.g., dissipativity/accretivity estimates, Lyapunov-type inequalities, or coercivity of an associated functional) and of the input dependence, that guarantee ISS of the resulting evolution with respect to inputs u ∈ L^∞(R_+, U).

(b) Apply the resulting framework to establish ISS (or appropriate variants such as integral ISS or strong ISS) for the porous medium equation and for the Navier–Stokes equations under physically meaningful classes of distributed and/or boundary disturbances.
artifact.status_search_result: A general ISS theory covering fully nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems via nonlinear semigroups, and applicable to the porous medium and Navier–Stokes equations under disturbances, does not appear to be established. Available literature focuses on linear or semilinear ISS results, or on stability of specific PDEs without an ISS-style robustness framework. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Input-to-state stability of infinite-dimensional systems: recent results and open questions
status_evidence.snippet: Survey lists ISS for fully nonlinear PDEs (porous medium, Navier–Stokes) as an open research direction requiring nonlinear semigroup methods.
status_evidence.claim: The development of general ISS methods for fully nonlinear PDEs is identified as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the Stability of Steady-State Solutions to the Navier–Stokes Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic stability of steady-state solutions of Navier–Stokes equations is studied, but not in an ISS-with-disturbance-input framework.
status_evidence.claim: Recent Navier–Stokes stability work does not provide an ISS framework with respect to L^∞ inputs.
